# A smaller invoice than the credit it names, settled the short way — the
# transaction named and nothing else, with the leftover declared.
#
# The customer's parked 100.00 USD covers this 40.00 invoice and leaves 60.00,
# so the credit is divided rather than attached whole. Dividing a credit is
# what a `from_credit:` block does; reached through a bare `txn_guid:` the same
# division has to do the same accounting, and the part left over has to keep
# the cost the credit was acquired at — 1.4 CAD/USD, the rate the first invoice
# was booked at — not a fresh rate for the day this invoice happens to be
# posted on. Priced at this invoice's own date it would be 1.37, and the book
# would report a gain the customer's money never made.
#
# Verified by tests/integration/test_foreign_currency_cost_basis.py.

invoice "INV-USD-THIRD"
	customer_id: "C-US"
	currency: USD
	date_opened: 2026-03-01
	entry:
		date: 2026-03-01
		description: "Short job"
		action: "Hours"
		account: "Income:Sales"
		quantity: 1
		price: 40
		taxable: false
		tax_included: false
	posted:
		date: 2026-03-01
		due: 2026-04-01
		ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
		memo: "Invoice INV-USD-THIRD"
		accumulate: true
	payment:
		date: 2026-03-01
		amount: 100
		bank_account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
		txn_guid: "TXN_GUID"
		prepayment: 60
		memo: "Part of the credit on account"
